title: The W. Ross Ashby journal and its indexes, read as a design source
paper_title: Ashby's journal as a specification: how much of it does this system's code implement?
paper_frame: Ashby kept a research journal for forty years and indexed it by concept. The index is a list of ideas he thought worth keeping; for a system built to be ultrastable it is a list of design questions. We bound each concept we use to code and count how many of them are bound.
kind: own R&D question set, regenerated from this system's records
data: doctrine/ashby-concepts.json: each concept restated in our own words, bound to code and linked to the archive's index page. The archive's text is not reproduced.
summary: The archive of Ashby's journal and card indexes is public. We took the concepts we could turn into mechanisms, stated each in our own words, linked it, and bound it to the code that implements it. Some index categories are not applied because they concern people or society, and the register says so.
limits: Source. The archive reserves all rights, so nothing in the journal is reproduced; each concept is paraphrased and linked. Which concepts are worth implementing is our judgment.
Binding. A concept is bound when each mechanism it names resolves to a file and marker here; it does not show the mechanism works, which is the job of the other papers.
Coverage. Index categories the register lists as not applied are excluded from the count and the reason is recorded.

misperception.belief: The classic cybernetics literature is history; it has nothing to say about modern AI systems.
misperception.counter: Ashby's concepts are specific enough to be implemented as code and checked: essential variables, step-functions, requisite variety, reducibility. A register that binds each concept to a mechanism shows how much of the theory a running system actually carries.

findings.concern: A concept in the register that the code does not carry
findings.claim: A concept named in the register is a claim that the code implements it. We read every mechanism the register names and count the concepts whose mechanisms all resolve in the repository.

mechanisms.how: each concept lists the mechanisms that implement it
the check fails when a mechanism or marker is gone
